description: List Google Drive files, newest change first. Filters combine with AND: `query` searches the full text and the name, `folder_ids` keeps files whose direct parent is one of those folders, and `mime_types` keeps files of those exact types (a folder is application/vnd.google-apps.folder). Trashed files are never returned. Shared drives are included. Pass `next_cursor` back as `cursor` for the next page; a null `next_cursor` ends the list.

query.description: Free text. Drive searches the file content and the name.

folder_ids.description: Keep only files whose direct parent is one of these folder ids.

mime_types.description: Keep only files of these exact mime types.

cursor.description: The next_cursor from the previous call. Omit for the first page.

limit.description: Files per page, 1 to 1000. Drive defaults to 100.

query.q: built by execute.ts from query + folder_ids + mime_types, always with trashed = false
query.fields: nextPageToken, files(id, name, mimeType, modifiedTime, version, webViewLink, parents)

response_schema.description: files.list. Lenient on purpose: Drive omits a field rather than sending null, adds fields between releases, and returns version as a string because it is an int64.

quirks.why_execute: Drive expresses all three filters in one `q` string with its own quoting rules, so the query is built in code. The provider ingress lives with it, because send_request takes a runtime validator.
quirks.query_escaping: Drive quotes values in single quotes and escapes with a backslash, so a searched phrase containing an apostrophe would otherwise be a syntax error.
quirks.shared_drives: supportsAllDrives and includeItemsFromAllDrives are both always sent: the first lets a shared-drive file appear, the second lets the call succeed once one does.
quirks.dropped_rows: An entry with no id, name, or mimeType is not a file anyone can act on, so it is dropped and the rest of the page is kept.
